The measured size (50.2 x 27.1 x 48.1) fits the brief's 49 long and 45 high.

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are all there: three legs (counted in the front, left and right views of sides.png, and in the motion frames) and one large eye on the front, about a third of the body's width. Nothing the brief names is missing. The brief names no claws, teeth or rivets, so their absence is not charged.

M4.reason: The body is yellowish, as the brief says, with a dark mottling. The eye is white with a black pupil, and the legs match the body. Colours are consistent across all ten views and the line-up. The pixel-noise texture is charged to M5, not here.

M5.reason: The body shows dappled mottling but no visible stripes, though the brief asks for striped and dappled hide (sides.png, all body views). Stripes show only as dark bands on the legs (attack.png, legs in every frame). The surface reads as coarse pixel noise rather than hide.

M6.reason: The brief's line-up test was caught twice of four readings (picked C when the asset was C, and B when it was B; picked D and A otherwise). Two catches is 'picked twice or more', which caps M6 at 1. The instruction to score M6 2 conflicts with the measurement, and the measurement is what may not be exceeded, so this is scored 1.

M7.reason: The eye is on the front, the body is upright, and the legs reach the floor line in the motion frames (motion.png, frames 0 and 13) with the feet on the origin. Nothing floats or leans off its stance in the views.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks pass with no errors. Triangles are 496, within twice the Half-Life median of 576. The legs meet the body and the feet touch the floor, and the eye sits in the body. The underside shows circular marks, but nothing is left open where the player can see it.

C1.reason: In the run (motion.png) every leg stays on the body and nothing sinks or floats. But the attack (attack.png, frames 0 to 7) shows almost no movement: the body and legs stay still and no blast or lift is visible, so the attack is not shown in motion as the brief describes.
